title: One Persistent Audio Player Replaces Three in Elvarika | vitalii.no
description:
How Elvarika went from three separate audio players that each forgot you the moment you left the page, to one that follows you everywhere and resumes exactly where you stopped.

Elvarika used to run three separate audio players — one for a learning session, one for a playlist, one for a 'premium' playlist view. Leaving a page to go look something else up would stop whatever you were listening to, and a saved playlist couldn't simply resume from where it left off.

The three players were removed and replaced with a single PlayerProvider that holds playback state in React context, a PlayerDock that renders the persistent controls, and a NowPlaying view for the current track — all backed by the browser's Media Session API so playback survives page navigation and shows proper lock-screen and notification controls. A review feature's audio hook now reads from that same provider instead of spinning up its own player, and playback position for saved playlists is kept in storage so a playlist picks back up where it left off.

Switching pages in Elvarika no longer interrupts whatever is playing, and a saved playlist now resumes exactly where you left it instead of starting over — three players down to one.
